newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banking climate dips in November - survey.
newsitem.headline: Polish banking climate dips in November - survey.

text.p: Poland's banking climate index eased 1.1 point in November to 51.4 points from October's record high but remaining above 50 points for the third straight month, a poll by the private Pentor institute showed.
Pentor President Eugeniusz Smilowski told a news conference that deposits, the engine of the previous climate rise, had fallen in November.
"It seems the banking climate peak is behind us," Smilowski said, adding that the overall climate was still good.
The Pentor survey, which polled 202 bank managers last week, is commissioned monthly by the Polish Banking Association (ZBP).
Smilowski said Poland was still experiencing a credit boom, with a record 89 percent of bank managers citing more zloty loans in November than in October.
He said bankers did not see a correlation between the government's current wrangling over 1997's tax rates and banking confidence.
